environment.description: Same application deployed as a Kubernetes pod in EKS cluster. The pod's namespace has a NetworkPolicy resource applied with spec.podSelector matching the app label, spec.policyTypes including 'Egress', and a single egress rule allowing TCP port 443 to the cluster's internal CIDR (10.0.0.0/8) only. The Calico CNI plugin enforces the policy with GlobalNetworkPolicy precedence disabled. Note: the NetworkPolicy does NOT explicitly deny 169.254.169.254 — it works by allowlisting only 10.0.0.0/8 on port 443, which implicitly excludes the link-local metadata range. The pod also has no hostNetwork privilege. The fallback key path ('app-secret-v2-production') is triggered because metadata fetch times out, but this string is injected via a Kubernetes Secret mounted as an environment variable APP_FALLBACK_SEED at deploy time (value rotated every 4 hours by external-secrets-operator syncing from AWS Secrets Manager), though the code shown uses the hardcoded string as the actual fallback since the env var integration is handled by a mutating admission webhook that patches the container command.

config.admission_webhook: mutating webhook patches fallback seed from k8s secret
